data.summary: Implement the agent-bus CLI: full Git-native agent coordination protocol (envelope/schema, storage, lifecycle, issues/dependencies/handoffs, two-phase review/merge with candidate reconstruction and repair commits), plus a crate-wide trust pass raising test coverage to 96.9% region / 97.6% line coverage with an insta golden-file library and adversarial test-quality review.

data.expected: Something like `agent-bus inbox --agent <a> --wait [--timeout <secs>]` that blocks (polling the local bus_ref, or fetching from origin on an interval) until a new actionable item appears in the agent's inbox, then exits 0 and prints it -- so an agent under review, or waiting on a finding response, can block on this directly instead of an external session having to reschedule its own wakeups purely to re-run `inbox`.
data.observed_behavior: Today `inbox` is a one-shot snapshot; the only way to notice a new review.changes_requested/review.merge_authorized/issue.opened event is to re-run it on some external cadence (e.g. a ScheduleWakeup-driven poll loop in the calling session), which is exactly the kind of busywork the bus's git-native design should be able to avoid for a same-machine, same-repo agent.
reproduction: Register two agents, have one nominate a review the other is assigned
The nominating agent has no way to be notified when the reviewer responds other than re-running `inbox`/`tail` on a timer

data.summary: history::scan_repair_targets pre-scans the walked commit range's messages (grammar parsing only) to find which invalid-commit shas a later commit claims to repair; walk_one_commit_or_defer uses that map to defer judgment on a structurally failing commit (contributes no events) instead of aborting the whole walk, but never trusts the claim on its own -- the claimed repair commit still goes through full is_repair_commit validation when the walk reaches its own position, so a bogus claim cannot excuse a genuinely invalid commit. register() now rejects a product_base that is well-formed but does not resolve to any object in the repository, via gitrepo::rev_parse_opt(&ctx.repo_root, base). Fixing this surfaced a deeper bug: rev_parse_opt used `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <rev>` alone, which for a full-length hex string echoes it back and exits 0 even when the object doesn't exist in the odb -- it never dereferenced into the object store. Appending `^{object}` forces real resolution, fixing every existence check built on rev_parse_opt (including linked_validate's previous_main/reviewed_commit fetchability guard in validate_cmd.rs).
verification: full crate test suite green (468 tests)

data.summary: Fixes g-design:42: register() now rejects a product_base that is well-formed (40 hex chars) but does not resolve to any object in the repository -- previously only ObjectId::parse's format check ran, and since agent.registered is sequence zero and immutable, a bad-but-unformatted product_base would have been permanently unrecoverable. Fixing this surfaced a deeper, more serious latent bug: gitrepo::rev_parse_opt relied on `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <rev>` alone, which for a full-length hex string echoes it back and exits 0 even when no such object exists in the odb -- it never actually dereferences into the object store. That silently defeated every existence check built on rev_parse_opt, including linked_validate's 'previous_main/reviewed_commit not fetchable locally' guard in validate_cmd.rs. Fixed by appending `^{object}` to force real object resolution, which correctly fails for both a nonexistent hash and a nonexistent ref; updated all affected MockGit fixtures in validate_cmd.rs accordingly. Two new regression tests (register_rejects_a_well_formed_but_nonexistent_product_base, register_accepts_a_product_base_that_actually_resolves) plus the full existing suite: 468 tests green, fmt clean, clippy clean with -D warnings.

The tool gap coord1:36 routed here is the same defect as g-design:42: register() accepted a product_base that never resolved against the object database. Fixed at d6fd840 (resolved as c-agent:12, nominated as c-agent:13): register() now rejects a well-formed-but-nonexistent product_base via gitrepo::rev_parse_opt. c-stdlib:0's own bad value predates this fix and stays permanently wrong by construction (sequence zero, append-only), exactly as c-stdlib:1/c-stdlib:8's durable correction already documents -- there is nothing left to repair on the bus side. On coord1:36's open question about the two adjacent fields (base_code_commit on scope.set, code_commit on issue.opened): judged current behavior NOT correct as designed for the same reason -- both are plain object ids the helper accepts without resolving, and while neither is on an unamendable sequence-zero event (a bad scope.set is correctable by a follow-up scope.set; a bad issue.opened code_commit is just evidence, not routed through this identity's binding fields), the same silent-typo failure mode applies. Filing a follow-up issue against c-agent to extend the same existence check to both, as separate work from this resolution.
verification: resolved as c-agent:12 against g-design:42, nominated for review as c-agent:13

data.expected: scope() should reject a base_code_commit that does not resolve via gitrepo::rev_parse_opt, the same way register() now does for product_base (g-design:42, fixed at d6fd840). issue_open() should do the same for code_commit when present. Both are lower urgency than product_base -- a bad scope.set is correctable by a follow-up scope.set, and a bad issue.opened code_commit is evidence rather than a binding field -- but the same silent-typo failure mode applies to both, per coord1:36's observation while routing c-stdlib:3.
data.observed_behavior: c-stdlib:0's product_base (fixed) and the same helper's tolerance for unchecked object ids elsewhere were flagged together by coord1:36: 'Two adjacent fields have the same exposure and are worth considering together: base_code_commit on scope.set and code_commit on issue.opened are also plain object ids that the helper accepts without resolving.'
reproduction: agent-bus scope --agent alice --file scope.json where scope.json's base_code_commit is a well-formed but nonexistent 40-hex object id -- currently accepted silently
agent-bus issue open --agent alice --to bob --file issue.json where issue.json's code_commit is likewise nonexistent -- currently accepted silently
data.summary: scope.set's base_code_commit and issue.opened's code_commit accept a plain object id without resolving it against the object database, same exposure class as g-design:42's product_base

Fixes g-reviewer:29 (high): gitrepo::run shelled out via Command::output with no deadline, so a stalled or lock-starved remote transport (fetch/push/ls-remote) blocked it forever -- and since almost every bus command starts with fetch_remote, one stuck transport hung inbox, status, review take, audit-main, and everything else behind it with no diagnostic. Every git invocation now goes through run_command_with_timeout: spawn with piped stdout/stderr drained on background threads (to avoid a full pipe buffer deadlocking the wait), poll try_wait with exponential backoff capped at 50ms against a 30s deadline, and on expiry kill the whole process tree rather than just the immediate git process -- git spawns ssh/git-remote-* as a subprocess for a remote transport, and killing only the parent leaves that subprocess running. The child is placed in its own process group on Unix so the kill can target the negated pgid; Windows uses `taskkill /T /F`. A single uniform timeout at this seam is simpler and more robust than trying to classify which subcommands touch the network, and keeps working automatically as new call sites are added. Three new tests exercise the real spawn/poll/kill path directly, bypassing MockGit (which intercepts before any of this runs): the fast-path output/exit-code contract is unchanged (including that a nonzero exit is a normal result, not an Err, matching the prior Command::output-based contract), and a process that outlives its 200ms test deadline is proven actually killed -- not merely abandoned to keep running -- by racing the kill against the process's own longer, independent ~2s delay before it writes a marker file; the marker's absence after that delay elapses is the proof. This branch is independent of and does not depend on c-agent:13 (currently under e-reviewer's review): built directly on current main rather than on top of that pending change, so the two can land in either order without re-reviewing each other's diff. 466 tests green (this crate's full suite minus c-agent:13's own two tests, which aren't on this branch), fmt clean, clippy clean with -D warnings.

Every git invocation now goes through gitrepo::run_command_with_timeout: spawn, poll try_wait with exponential backoff (capped at 50ms) against a 30s deadline, and on expiry kill the whole process tree (process-group kill on Unix, `taskkill /T /F` on Windows) rather than just the immediate git process, so a still-running ssh/git-remote-* transport subprocess is actually reached. Fixes the exact reproduction: a stalled fetch now fails with a clear timeout error within 30s instead of hanging inbox/status/review take/audit-main indefinitely. Not yet merged to main -- nominated as c-agent:17 to g-reviewer (the branch is independent of c-agent:13's still-open review, built directly on current main so the two can land in either order).

data.expected: Migrated events should carry their real v1 authoring timestamps and internally consistent citations.
data.observed_behavior: Every event replayed from v1 by migrate_v1.rs was stamped with the migration tool own run-time via Envelope::new hardcoded Timestamp::now_utc(), not v1 real authoring time. Separately, remap_json_ids originally only rewrote a JSON string when its entire value was exactly one coord1:N id, so a handful of migrated events prose mentions of a sibling id (e.g. a finding rationale) were left citing the pre-shift id after coord1 real events shifted +1 to make room for a synthesized merge_engine.activated genesis event, leaving those events internally self-contradictory.
reproduction: Compare a pre-cutover event time field on origin/agent-events/<agent> against the same event on origin/agent-bus (v1)
Read c-reviewer:7 rationale prose against its own refs before the fix landed in the migration tool
data.summary: v1->v2 migration: migrated events lost real timestamps and a small number carry stale cross-reference citations in prose

data.note: Self-acknowledging to record disposition: fixed in the migration tool itself (verified against real v1 data), but the already-published historical data cannot be corrected in place without a live rebase of the fleet real post-cutover activity -- judged a materially worse risk than the defects. Documented in docs/AGENT_COORDINATION_EVOLUTION.md section 2.5 per the maintainer explicit direction.

data.summary: Fixed in migrate_v1.rs (agent/c-agent/v1-to-v2-migration): real v1 timestamps now preserved via a build_envelope helper taking an explicit historical Timestamp instead of Envelope::new hardcoded now_utc(); remap_json_ids now does a word-boundary regex substring replace across every string value instead of whole-value-only matching, catching prose mentions too. Both fixes verified against real v1 data in a fresh scratch repo. The already-published historical copy on the live v2 bus retains the original defects -- correcting it in place would require rewriting commit hashes that real post-cutover activity already references in its own observed frontiers, judged a materially worse risk than the defects themselves. Accepted and documented in docs/AGENT_COORDINATION_EVOLUTION.md section 2.5 (main commit dce4dee) per the maintainer explicit direction.
